common_name: Mark Jury Magnolia (New Zealand Breeder-Parent Hybrid Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant grafted, container-grown trees in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, in a sheltered site protected from spring frost pockets; Mark Jury is grown chiefly as a breeding parent and is far less commonly offered than the named hybrids raised from it.

directions: Mark Jury arrived at Felix Jury's Taranaki, New Zealand nursery as an unplanned seedling received from Hillier Nurseries in England, thought to be a hybrid of Magnolia campbellii var. mollicomata 'Lanarth' with M. sargentiana robusta, and Felix named it for his youngest son after recognizing its value as a breeding parent. Its own very large flowers open pale lavender-pink fading toward white with pronounced recurved petals, a softer color than the solid deep purple of true 'Lanarth', on a vigorous tree that eventually makes an impressive specimen for a large garden or park rather than a typical residential lot. Felix used it as the pollen parent behind several of his best-known hybrids, including 'Iolanthe' (crossed onto Magnolia x soulangeana 'Lennei'), making it a foundational but seldom-grown ancestor behind the modern Jury magnolia hybrids. Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, sheltered from spring frost pockets that can damage early flower buds.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)
Tikorangi: The Jury Garden plant records

common_name: Goldstrike Azalea (Compact Fragrant Golden Native Hybrid Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this compact Aromi hybrid stays noticeably smaller than its larger parent 'Appalachian Gold'.

directions: Goldstrike is one of Dr. Eugene Aromi's golden-flowered native hybrid azalea introductions, bred in Mobile, Alabama, and later used alongside 'Appalachian Gold' as a parent of the more compact 'Dancing Rabbit.' It bears fragrant yellow blooms opening from red-orange buds on a notably compact, rounded shrub, smaller than many other Aromi hybrids and well suited to foundation plantings or smaller woodland-edge beds. Like its Aromi relatives it carries Gulf Coast heat and humidity tolerance from its native Rhododendron austrinum-derived breeding line. Plant in humus-rich, acidic, evenly moist soil in partial shade, and mulch well to protect the shallow root system through summer heat.
